title: Optical PLL Research Intern
summary:
About Taara:
Born at X, Google's Moonshot Factory, Taara is on a mission to connect billions of people lacking abundant and affordable internet today by pioneering the way we use light to deliver faster, cheaper, more reliable connectivity. We are bringing groundbreaking wireless optical communication and photonics chip technologies to the world to bridge the digital divide.
Joining Taara allows you to work as part of a multidisciplinary team of experts in optics, software, and hardware, all collaborating to solve the hardest connectivity challenges on a global scale. If you want to tackle problems that matter and build tools with real-world impact, we would love to meet you.
About the Role:
As an Optical PLL Research Intern, you will lay the groundwork for an integrated optical phase-locked loop (OPLL) that locks an external laser for coherent reception in next-generation wireless optical links. This is a long-term project spanning lab and simulation, ideally a year or more. It could also anchor a thesis or a longer-term collaboration.
What such a loop can achieve is bounded by real components. You will evaluate lasers, modulators, and analog electronics, build benchtop experiments around them, and work toward a stable closed loop. In parallel, you will extend our simulation and use the two to check each other.
There is genuine room to shape the direction. Survey what is available, design your own experiments, and follow the evidence to the strongest design.
How you will make 10X Impact:
- Component Evaluation: Screen commercial lasers, modulators, and photodetectors. Measure what vendors do not publish.
- Loop Design: Design the loops that track carrier phase and frequency, and validate them against control theory.
- Chip Requirements: Define what the integrated OPLL needs from its laser, electronics, and loop.
- Physical-Layer Simulation: Extend our model of the link and reconcile it with measurement.

As a Research Intern, you'll own a real research question rather than a ticket. - Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Statistics, or Linguistics

- Ability to move quickly in a zero-to-one environment

- A track record of research contributions, such as first-author publications at major ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) or strong journals.
